subject: Request: Country-locked hosting matrix & private endpoint flow — Brookline Health
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.s@brooklinehealth.com>

Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@brooklinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Country-locked hosting matrix & private endpoint flow — Brookline Health

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this — Brookline's compliance team has a few gating items as we evaluate Redwood for PHI-adjacent inference workloads. Can you provide: 

- A country-locked hosting matrix that shows where data and compute live for hosted/dedicated/private modes (need explicit tie to physical region and whether egress may cross borders).
- A diagram or short doc that explains the private endpoint / peering options you offer (Privatelink, VPC peering, Transit Gateway) and where traffic termination happens (customer VPC vs Redwood-managed).
- Clarification on KMS options: do you support BYOK and can keys be provisioned in our account/region? Any isolation guarantees for keys used for tenant crypto?
- Link to the latest SOC 2 report and SIG/CAIQ answers relevant to network segregation and key management.

We also have a handful of specific requirements: 1) all inference requests for our EU and APAC users must terminate on servers located in the corresponding region, 2) audit logs must be retained for 7 years and made available for export, 3) a single-tenant keystore option for the dedicated offering.

Would prefer a written packet we can attach to our procurement docs; happy to schedule a short call if that's easier. Attaching our compliance checklist for context.

Best,
Tara Singh
Head of Compliance, Brookline Health
T: +1 415 555 0129

Attachments: brookline_requirements_2026-05.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Subject: Re: Country-locked hosting matrix & private endpoint flow — Brookline Health

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear list. I've started a short packet for you and attached a first-pass residency matrix. Quick summary up front:

- Residence: Redwood supports region-restricted routing in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. The attached matrix maps each mode to physical region(s) and whether storage/compute/keys can be constrained to that region.
- Private connectivity: we support three termination modes — PrivateLink (endpoint in customer VPC), Direct Peering (Redwood-private router in customer VPC via partner), and Dedicated Interconnect (for large customers). The attached flow diagram highlights where traffic terminates and where ephemeral caches/KV may exist.
- KMS: we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS including HSM-backed keys. Keys may be provisioned in the customer's cloud account and scoped per-tenant; for Dedicated we can offer single-tenant keystore options.
- Audit logs: we provide configurable retention; for Hosted we can export logs to your S3/GCS/Azure blob for long-term retention. For Dedicated/Private we support direct write-to-customer logging endpoints and can meet the 7-year export requirement.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick 30-minute call to walk the packet and confirm the termination mode you'd prefer, 2) if you want KMS BYOK we'll need an operations worksheet (I can send a template), 3) I'll pull the SOC2/CAIQ/SIG references and include pointer links in the packet.

I've attached: redwood_residency_matrix_v1.xlsx and a PNG export of the private endpoint flow (redwood_private_endpoint_flow_v2.drawio.png). Will follow up with the SOC2 links.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect — Compliance & Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_residency_matrix_v1.xlsx (Excel, 120KB); redwood_private_endpoint_flow_v2.drawio.png (PNG, 250KB)

Thanks — received the matrix and the flow diagram. A couple clarifying items before we take the call: 

1) For BYOK: Brookline requires tenant keys to be single-tenant and kept in our account for APAC and EU scopes specifically; multi-tenant keys are only acceptable for US workloads. Can your Dedicated offering guarantee the single-tenant keystore isolation in APAC?

2) Caching: we understand you use prefix/KV cache to speed inference. We need confirmation that cache contents for region-locked requests will not be replicated outside the region and that persisted artifacts are deleted on-demand.

3) Audit export: we'll need an automated export into our GCS bucket with a signed assertion that exported logs include per-token routing metadata (timestamp, model, route id, region).

If those are possible, please include language we can attach to procurement; if not possible, call them out.

Availability for a call: Monday 18 May between 9–11am PT.

Tara

Hi Tara — apologies for the slight delay. Answers below (I'll add formal language to the packet and send before the call):

1) Dedicated keystore isolation (APAC/EU): yes — for Dedicated we can provision a single-tenant HSM-backed keystore scoped to your tenant and provisioned in your cloud account/region. That keystore is not shared with other customers and access is controlled via customer-managed IAM policies. We'll add the specific wording suitable for procurement (keystore SLA and isolation statement).

2) Caching: regional caching is supported. Prefix/KV caches used by the runtime are sharded by tenancy + region. We do not replicate caches across regions for region-locked workloads; ephemeral caches are stored on local SSD in the serving zone and cleared on instance termination. For persisted artifacts (logs, model shard caches), Redwood provides deletion APIs and we can include a contractual procedure for on-demand deletion and verification logs.

3) Audit export: automated export to a customer GCS/S3 is supported. The export schema includes per-request metadata: timestamp (UTC), model_id, route_id, region, token_count, and request_id. We'll produce a signed attestation describing the fields and retention pipeline you can attach to procurement.

I've uploaded the SOC 2 Type II summary and a condensed CAIQ network section to our secure drive; links below. I'll send formal procurement wording (keystore isolation wording + audit export wording) and a short ops worksheet to collect your cloud account IDs before the call.

Links: https://redwood.example.com/soc2/report-2025 
https://drive.example.com/redwood/caiaq-condensed-network

Available for the Monday 18 May window you suggested — propose 9:30am PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and an operations worksheet.

Best,
Priyom
